newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-PONTING STAKES TEST CLAIM WITH CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING STAKES TEST CLAIM WITH CENTURY.

text.p: Ricky Ponting staked a claim for a place in Australia's team for next week's fourth Test when he blasted an unbeaten 126 in his country's 369 for four declared against English county championship leaders Glamorgan on Wednesday.
Tasmanian Ponting reached his first century of the tour off 135 balls with 13 fours and when he moved on to 123 he passed 5,000 first-class career runs.
Justin Langer, also in the running for the number six spot at Headingly, hit 50 not out off 75 balls in an unbeaten stand with Ponting of 123.

Glamorgan captain Matthew Maynard decided to field after winning the toss despite the absence of front-line bowlers Robert Croft, who was rested, and Waqar Younis and Steve Watkin, who were both injured.
It looked a bad move as Mark Taylor and Matthew Elliott quickly put on 72 in 18 overs for the first wicket before Elliott was caught at slip for 26.
Taylor went on to reach 71 before being caught on the boundary while Greg Blewett hit 54 off 100 balls with 10 fours before playing on.
Michael Slater continued to struggle, managing only 26 before he tried to cut Cosker and edged to wicket keeper Colin Metson, playing his first first-class match of the summer.
